assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).

novel.justification: This project-specific global entropy condition is satisfied by smooth compact administrative boundaries, including the circular witnesses, and directly controls the number of boundary locations that every covering and chaining upper bound must handle; it imposes no local Ahlfors measure condition.

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).

standard.name: Lipschitz regression smoothness on the observed design support
bounded Hölder-ball envelope for the regression trace

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal L_P(Y-g_{t,P}(X)\mid X=z)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\).
\(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: The common two-sided boundary modulus is project-specific and is realized by geographic designs whose score density vanishes polynomially with inward normal distance along an administrative boundary; Gaiffas2005Degenerate motivates polynomial design degeneracy only in a one-dimensional pointwise problem.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(C_mh^{\kappa}\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: The envelope is realized by a single polynomial density zero on an otherwise positive tubular design and formalizes isolated geographic access bottlenecks without restricting response smoothness.
A persistent isolated thin site occurs where a smooth boundary meets one lake, pass, or data-redaction pocket, and the circular witness gives an explicit law with this property.

Boundary-wide sampling depletion arises when residence or measurement density vanishes with normal distance from an entire administrative border, and the symmetric tubular witness realizes the condition exactly.

assumptions.condition: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: A declared common modulus records the weakest two-sided local information available along the boundary and can be estimated from score-only pilot data in geographic designs.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: A lower packing envelope describes guaranteed multiplicity of sparse boundary segments and is directly realized by repeated tubular depletion.

definitions.name: nonempty triangular profile union
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)=\bigcup_{(\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\in\Lambda_n}\{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}:\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\text{ for every }0<h\le h_0\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}\). The declared domain of \(\Lambda_n\) requires this union to be nonempty.

definitions.name: empirical one-sided counts
definitions.construction: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_n\).

definitions.name: count-adaptive bandwidth
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: mass-adaptive boundary trace estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

definitions.name: expected-sup minimax risk
definitions.construction: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.

definitions.name: explicit circular thinning witnesses
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

definitions.name: two-sided scale-dependent tent family
definitions.construction: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) by the same formulas with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\), and \(\psi_{1,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_{\star})/h)_+\). In each family, \(g_{1,P}(z)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(g_{0,P}(z)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(\theta_{1,P}(x)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\), and \(\theta_{0,P}(x)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\).

definitions.name: arbitrary-modulus optimal-recovery handle
definitions.construction: Use the count-qualified local-constant estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) on \(\mathcal H_n\), clipped to \([-2L,2L]\). Its global upper guarantee is obtained from the lower mass modulus \(m\), empirical one-sided counts \(N_{t,n}\), and global boundary entropy. Its converse uses radius-\(h/3\) Lipschitz tents at \(h\)-separated thin sites certified by \(\mathsf J_{-}\) and finite-information testing inside \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

definitions.name: thickness-adaptive honest-band handle
definitions.construction: Condition on the observed scores and calibrate all nonempty side averages over the finite disk-pattern family by the conditional tail radius supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), whose moment-generating-function bound is derived from the exact conditional Gaussian assumption; add the Lipschitz bias \(L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) at a positive selected count and the trace envelope \(L\) at a zero count, then difference the two sides to form \(\mathcal C_n\). For any two full observed laws, transfer simultaneous coverage between them with \(\operatorname{TV}\) to obtain the two-law expected-half-width obstruction. This handle does not perform local multiplicity calibration and does not replace full-observed-law distinguishability by score-only distinguishability.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the target a unique observed-side trace rather than a version-dependent conditional mean at a null boundary point.
statements.gap: HahnToddVanDerKlaauw2001 identifies regression-discontinuity limits under continuity, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance studies the boundary curve; this node records identification on vanishing-support sides without assigning a conditional mean at the boundary itself.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can interpret the fitted jump as an observed-law-identified causal trace contrast even when the score has zero density on the boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and define the finite Borel measure
\[
 \mu_t(E):=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t),
 \qquad E\subseteq\mathbb R^2\text{ Borel}.
 \tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\), this law satisfies each of the seven assumptions listed in that definition. In particular, the polynomial lower-mass, Lipschitz, bounded-trace, Gaussian-error, sharp-assignment, and consistency conditions used below all hold.

We first show that every boundary point belongs to both one-sided supports. Fix \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(r>0\), and set
\[
 h:=\min\{h_0,r/2\}.
\]
Because \(h_0>0\), one has \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(h<r\). Since \(c_m>0\), \(\kappa>2\), and \(\mathrm{ass:polynomial\text{-}lower\text{-}mass}\) holds,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mu_t(B(x,r))
 &\ge P\{X\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X,x)\le h\}\\
 &=q_{t,P}(x,h)\\
 &\ge c_m h^\kappa>0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus every open neighborhood of \(x\) has positive \(\mu_t\)-mass. By the definition of the support of a Borel measure,
\[
 x\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu_t)=\mathcal X_{t,P}.
 \tag{3}
\]
This proves (3) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\) and both values of \(t\).

Put
\[
 \delta_{\mathcal B}(z):=\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x),
 \qquad
 U_{t,P}:=\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The triangle inequality gives
\[
 |\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)-\delta_{\mathcal B}(z')|\le d(z,z'),
 \tag{5}
\]
so \(U_{t,P}\) is relatively open in \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\). For \(x\in\mathcal B\), (3) and \(\delta_{\mathcal B}(x)=0<h_0\) imply \(x\in U_{t,P}\). If \(z\to x\) with \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), then eventually \(z\in U_{t,P}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\) gives
\[
 |g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(x)|\le Ld(z,x)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently the defining trace limit exists uniquely and satisfies
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)
 =\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)
 =g_{t,P}(x).
 \tag{6}
\]

We next verify local integrability and identify the pointwise Lipschitz representative. For every \(z\in U_{t,P}\), compactness of \(\mathcal B\) yields \(x_z\in\mathcal B\) such that \(d(z,x_z)=\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)\). By (3), (6), \(\mathrm{ass:lipschitz\text{-}side\text{-}means}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:bounded\text{-}side\text{-}traces}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |g_{t,P}(z)|
 &\le |g_{t,P}(x_z)|+Ld(z,x_z)\\
 &=|\theta_{t,P}(x_z)|+L\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)\\
 &\le L(1+h_0).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
The complement of \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(\mu_t)\) is a union of open \(\mu_t\)-null sets. Since \(\mathbb R^2\) has a countable base, that complement is a countable union of such sets, and hence
\[
 \mu_t(\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal X_{t,P})=0.
 \tag{8}
\]
Let \(\varepsilon_t:=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) on the one-sided support. By \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}regression\text{-}moments}\), outside a \(P_X\)-null subset of \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Equations (7)--(9), followed by integration with respect to \(P_X\), imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E_P\!\left[|Y|\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_t,\ \delta_{\mathcal B}(X)<h_0\}\right]\\
 &\quad\le
 \int_{\mathcal A_t\cap U_{t,P}}
 \left(|g_{t,P}(z)|+\mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\right)P_X(dz)\\
 &\quad\le
 \{L(1+h_0)+\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}\}\,\mu_t(U_{t,P})<\infty.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
For every bounded Borel function \(b:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\), absolute integrability from (9) and conditional centering give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E_P\!\left[b(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_t\cap U_{t,P}\}
       \{Y-g_{t,P}(X)\}\right]\\
 &\quad=
 \int_{\mathcal A_t\cap U_{t,P}}b(z)
       \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]P_X(dz)=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{11}
\]
Therefore \(g_{t,P}|_{U_{t,P}}\) is a representative of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\), restricted to \(U_{t,P}\). The model's Lipschitz condition gives
\[
 |g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z'),
 \qquad z,z'\in U_{t,P}.
 \tag{12}
\]

To prove pointwise uniqueness, let \(f_1,f_2:U_{t,P}\to\mathbb R\) be two \(L\)-Lipschitz representatives of this restricted equivalence class. Then
\[
 f_1=f_2\qquad \mu_t\text{-almost everywhere on }U_{t,P}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Suppose instead that for some \(z\in U_{t,P}\),
\[
 \Delta:=|f_1(z)-f_2(z)|>0.
\]
Because \(L>0\) and \(\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\), choose
\[
 0<r<\min\left\{h_0-\delta_{\mathcal B}(z),\frac{\Delta}{4L}\right\}.
\]
By (5),
\[
 B(z,r)\cap\mathcal X_{t,P}\subseteq U_{t,P}.
 \tag{14}
\]
For every \(z'\) in this relative ball, the triangle inequality and the two Lipschitz inequalities yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |f_1(z')-f_2(z')|
 &\ge \Delta-|f_1(z')-f_1(z)|-|f_2(z')-f_2(z)|\\
 &\ge \Delta-2Ld(z,z')>\frac{\Delta}{2}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{15}
\]
Since \(z\in\operatorname{supp}(\mu_t)\), the definition of support and (8) give
\[
 \mu_t(B(z,r)\cap\mathcal X_{t,P})
 =\mu_t(B(z,r))>0.
 \tag{16}
\]
Equations (14)--(16) contradict (13). Hence the Lipschitz representative is pointwise unique on \(U_{t,P}\); by (6), its boundary trace is unique as well.

Now let \(P,P'\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) induce the same observed law of \(O=(Y,X)\) under the same known assignment geometry. Their \(X\)-marginals, one-sided restricted measures (1), supports, and sets (4) coincide. By (10), the relevant locally restricted outcomes are integrable under both laws. Their conditional-regression equivalence classes on that common set therefore coincide because those classes are determined by the common joint law of \((Y,X)\). Pointwise uniqueness gives
\[
 g_{t,P}|_{U_{t,P}}=g_{t,P'}|_{U_{t,P'}}.
\]
Taking boundary limits in (6) gives \(\theta_{t,P}=\theta_{t,P'}\). Since, by definition,
\[
 \tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P},
\]
one also has \(\tau_P=\tau_{P'}\). Thus the near-boundary regression representative, each boundary trace, and their contrast are observed-law functionals, without choosing a conditional-mean version at a null boundary point.

It remains to establish the potential-outcome compatibility. Define
\[
 S_t:=\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\},
 \qquad
 D_t:=S_t\cap\{z:\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Because \(D_t\subseteq\mathcal A_t\), while \(D_t\cap\mathcal X_{t,P}\subseteq U_{t,P}\), equation (8) gives
\[
 P_X(D_t\setminus U_{t,P})=0.
 \tag{18}
\]
Equations (7), (9), (10), and (18) show that \(g_{t,P}(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\) and \(Y\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\) are integrable. On \(\{X\in D_t\}\), the definition of \(S_t\) and \(\mathrm{ass:sharp\text{-}assignment}\) imply \(T=t\); then \(\mathrm{ass:consistency}\) implies \(Y=Y(t)\). Hence \(Y(t)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\) is integrable as well.

Let \(p_t:=P_X(D_t)\). If \(p_t>0\), define the probability law obtained by normalization to this intersection by
\[
 Q_t(C):=\frac{P(C\cap\{X\in D_t\})}{p_t}.
 \tag{19}
\]
The division is valid because \(p_t>0\). For every bounded Borel function \(b:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\), the established integrability, the equality \(Y=Y(t)\) on \(\{X\in D_t\}\), (11), and (18) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{Q_t}[b(X)\{Y(t)-g_{t,P}(X)\}]
 &=\frac{1}{p_t}\mathbb E_P\!\left[b(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}
       \{Y(t)-g_{t,P}(X)\}\right]\\
 &=\frac{1}{p_t}\mathbb E_P\!\left[b(X)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}
       \{Y-g_{t,P}(X)\}\right]\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{20}
\]
Indeed, the last equality is (11) applied with the bounded Borel multiplier \(b\mathbf 1_{D_t}\), with the \(P_X\)-null discrepancy in (18) removed. The defining integral characterization of conditional expectation now yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_t}[Y(t)\mid X]=g_{t,P}(X),
 \qquad Q_t\text{-almost surely}.
 \tag{21}
\]
Equivalently, the claimed equality holds \(P_X\)-almost everywhere on \(D_t\). If \(p_t=0\), that compatibility assertion is vacuous.

Finally, if \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), then \(S_0=\mathcal A_0\) and \(S_1=\mathcal A_1\). Thus
\[
 D_t=\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\delta_{\mathcal B}(z)<h_0\},
\]
and (21) holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube. Only \(Y(t)\mathbf 1\{X\in D_t\}\) was required to be integrable, so no integrability condition was imposed on the counterfactual away from its observed side.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>2\), there are constants \(0<c_\kappa<C_\kappa<\infty\) such that \(c_\kappa h^{\kappa}\le\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))\le C_\kappa h^{\kappa}\) for all sufficiently small \(h\). In particular, the local-mass exponent is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).
statements.justification: This calculation is the geometry kill test on which every polynomial-thickness rate depends.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate calibrates rates to a one-dimensional design density, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance does not calculate polynomial horn mass.
statements.consumer: Support diagnostics for geographic boundary designs can translate a measured horn cross-section into the correct effective-sample-size exponent.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}horn}\), a vertical section of \(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\) at inward coordinate \(u\) has length \(2u^{\kappa-1}\). Since \(B(0,h)\subset\{0<u<h\}\times[-h,h]\), Tonelli's theorem for the nonnegative section indicator gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2\{\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h)\}
 \le 2\int_0^h u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
For \(0<u<h/2\), one has \(h^2-u^2\ge3h^2/4\). Because \(\kappa>2\), for all sufficiently small \(h<h_0\),
\[
 u^{\kappa-1}\le(h/2)^{\kappa-1}\le \sqrt{3}h/2.
\]
Hence the entire section \(\{|v|\le u^{\kappa-1}\}\) lies in \(B(0,h)\), and another application of Tonelli gives
\[
 \operatorname{Leb}_2\{\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h)\}
 \ge 2\int_0^{h/2}u^{\kappa-1}\,du
 =\frac{2^{1-\kappa}}{\kappa}h^{\kappa}.
\]
Thus one may take \(c_{\kappa}=2^{1-\kappa}/\kappa\) and \(C_{\kappa}=2/\kappa\). Both are positive and finite, and the power is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).

statements.statement: Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).
statements.justification: The explicit circular laws prove nonemptiness and make the same-modulus, different-multiplicity comparison a legal within-model construction.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2009Uniform and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 analyze finitely many zeros in univariate regression, but neither supplies two symmetric assignment sides or a boundary-wide circular depletion witness.
statements.consumer: Simulation modules for \(\texttt{rd2d}\) can reproduce both designs from normalized score densities rather than relying on an informal horn sketch.
statements.proof_tex:
Write a point of the circular tube as
\[
 z=(1+s)(\cos\phi,\sin\phi),\qquad |s|\le h_0,quad 0\le\phi<2\pi.
\]
Because \(h_0<1\), these are nonsingular coordinates with area element \((1+s)\,ds\,d\phi\). Hence the pervasive normalizing constant from \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\) is
\[
 Z_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
 =2\pi\int_{-h_0}^{h_0}|s|^{\kappa-2}(1+s)\,ds
 =\frac{4\pi}{\kappa-1}h_0^{\kappa-1}.
\]
It is positive and finite uniformly for \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\). The isolated integrand is nonnegative, bounded by one, and positive except at one point. Dominated convergence on the compact closure \([2,\overline\kappa]\), together with compactness of \(\mathcal T\), therefore bounds its normalizer uniformly away from zero and infinity.

On a sufficiently small coordinate patch about any \(x\in S^1\), let \(s\) be signed normal depth and \(v\) signed arclength. Compactness of \(S^1\) and \(h_0<1\) give constants, uniform in \(x\) and \(\kappa\), for which the Jacobian is bounded above and below and
\[
 c(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}\le d(z,x)\le C(s^2+v^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently, on either assignment side and for all sufficiently small \(h\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(x,h)
 &\asymp \int_0^h\int_{-\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}^{\sqrt{h^2-s^2}}
 s^{\kappa-2}\,dv\,ds\\
 &=h^{\kappa}\int_0^1 2w^{\kappa-2}\sqrt{1-w^2}\,dw
 \asymp h^{\kappa}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{1}
\]
The last integral is positive and is bounded above and below uniformly on \([2,\overline\kappa]\). Compactness and positivity allow the constants to be enlarged so that (1) holds for every \(0<h\le h_0\). Choose \(c_m>0\) below the uniform lower constant and \(C_m>c_m\) above the uniform upper constant. Every boundary point then belongs to the thin set at level \(C_mh^{\kappa}\). If \(E\) is a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(S^1\), disjoint-arc and covering-arc comparisons with total arclength \(2\pi\) give
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |E|\le C h^{-1}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}. \tag{2}
\]

For the isolated density put \(s_x=d(x,x_{\star})\). The same coordinate comparison gives, uniformly in the side \(t\),
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\ge
 \begin{cases}
 c h^{\kappa},&s_x\le2h,\\
 c h^2\min\{1,(s_x/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\},&s_x>2h.
 \end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
For the first line, integrate over a side-specific subball of radius proportional to \(h\) whose distance from \(x_{\star}\) is proportional to \(h\). For the second, use a subball of radius \(h/2\) about \(x\) and the triangle inequality. Since \(s_x>2h\) in the second line and \(h_0<1\), both lines are at least a uniform constant times \(h^{\kappa}\). At \(x=x_{\star}\), polar integration on either side also yields
\[
 q_{t,P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x_{\star},h)
 \le C\int_0^h r^{\kappa-2}r\,dr
 \le C'h^{\kappa}. \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4) prove the common polynomial lower-mass condition and the asserted equivalence at \(x_{\star}\).

If \(a_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(x,h)\le u\), (3) implies, after enlarging a uniform constant to cover the case in which the right side exceeds the circle's diameter,
\[
 s_x\le C\left\{h+(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
An arc of the length on the right of (5) contains at most
\[
 C\left\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\right\}
\]
points separated by \(h\). This is \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\), after enlarging \(C_{\mathrm{iso}}\). At \(u=C_mh^{\kappa}\), this upper bound is constant, while (4) puts \(x_{\star}\) in the thin set. Hence
\[
 \mathsf J_{P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}}(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1. \tag{6}
\]
The estimates extend to the remaining compact range of radii by changing constants. The circle satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) by the same arc argument. The exponent in (1) and (4) is also consistent with \(\mathrm{lem:polynomial\text{-}horn\text{-}mass}\).

Finally, the assignment is sharp by construction, the displayed potential-outcome formula gives consistency, and independence of the Gaussian variables gives \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\). Both observed-side regressions and traces are zero, so the Lipschitz and trace-envelope properties hold. Equations (1)--(6) and the class definitions prove
\[
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}.
\]

statements.statement: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).
statements.justification: This lemma certifies the packed lower experiment inside the same classes used by the upper bounds and states its pairwise information budget.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate uses local univariate bumps, while the present family perturbs both identified boundary sides at many separated sites without changing the common score-mass modulus.
statements.consumer: The minimax lower theorem can invoke a concrete Fano family for pervasive thinning and a concrete Le Cam pair for isolated thinning.
statements.proof_tex:
The distance map \(z\mapsto d(z,x_j)\) is one-Lipschitz. Thus \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\) is \(h^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, and each perturbed side regression in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz. Its absolute trace is at most \(Lh/4\le L\) for sufficiently small \(h\). The perturbation changes neither the score law nor any local-mass or packing property. The conditional Gaussian-error, sharp-assignment, and consistency properties follow directly from the construction. Therefore \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) and the class definitions put every pervasive perturbation in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and both isolated perturbations in \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\).

Maximality of the \(3h\)-separated set implies that arcs of radius \(3h\) cover \(S^1\), while arcs of radius \(3h/2\) about its points are disjoint. Comparing their total arclength with \(2\pi\) gives
\[
 c h^{-1}\le |\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\le C h^{-1}. \tag{7}
\]

Put \(a=Lh/4\). Conditional on \(X=z\), the relevant Gaussian coordinates under alternatives \(j\) and \(k\) have common variance \(\sigma^2\), and their mean difference has absolute value \(a|\psi_{j,h}(z)-\psi_{k,h}(z)|\). Direct integration gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2),\mathcal N(\nu,\sigma^2)\}
 =\frac{(\mu-\nu)^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{8}
\]
The integrand vanishes outside \(B(x_j,h)\cup B(x_k,h)\). The coordinate calculations in the witness-membership proof give
\[
 \int_{B(x_j,h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa},
 \qquad
 \int_{B(x_{\star},h)}f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)\,dz\le Ch^{\kappa}.
\]
Since \(0\le\psi_{j,h}\le1\), conditioning on \(X\) in (8), and summing the two potential-outcome coordinates if the superpopulation experiment is used, gives in either family
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h},\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h})
 \le \frac{Ca^2h^{\kappa}}{\sigma^2}
 \le \frac{CL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{9}
\]
The observed-data divergence is no larger, by marginalization. For the displayed product measures, likelihood ratios factor, so relative entropy is additive. Thus
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\otimes n},
 \mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\otimes n})
 \le \frac{CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}}{\sigma^2}. \tag{10}
\]
At an active center, \(\psi_{j,h}(x_j)=1\). The trace formulas in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\) yield
\[
 \theta_{1,P}(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-\frac{Lh}{4},\qquad
 \tau_P(x_j)=\frac{Lh}{2}.
\]
Together with (7) and (10), these are all the asserted properties.

statements.statement: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies multiplicity of thin locations, rather than local mass at the single worst point, as the missing information coordinate for uniform boundary estimation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially normalized univariate sup-norm estimator under a positive continuous design density, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies known-design global \(L^2\) loss; none gives a same-modulus isolated-versus-pervasive expected-sup separation for a two-sided causal boundary.
statements.consumer: Users of the full boundary causal trace curve can distinguish one local data desert from boundary-wide depletion before interpreting a worst-case uniform rate.
statements.proof_tex:
For a law \(P\), define the finite one-sided score measure
\[
 \mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t).
\]
If \(P\) belongs to either displayed class, \(x\in\mathcal B\), and \(r>0\), put \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\). The polynomial lower-mass property inherited from the corresponding class definition gives
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}
 \ge q_{t,P}(x,s)
 \ge c_ms^{\kappa}>0. \tag{23}
\]
Thus every boundary point belongs to \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\). The model-class Lipschitz property makes the distinguished representative continuous there, so the trace definition gives
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x),
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B. \tag{24}
\]
Because \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), sharp assignment makes \(X\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T=t\). Thus all side averages below have conditional observed-outcome mean \(g_{t,P}(X)\). Consistency supplies the causal interpretation of the resulting trace contrast; the risk calculations concern its identified observed-law functional.

We first prove the lower bounds by experiments contained in the stated classes. Begin with any member of the nonempty class under consideration, retain its score law and geometry, take independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and set \(Y(s)=\sigma Z_s\) for \(s\in\{0,1\}\). Call the resulting law \(Q_0\). Its side regressions and traces vanish. All design conditions are unchanged, its traces obey the envelope, and its observed residual is conditionally \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\), so \(Q_0\) remains in the same class.

For the isolated class let
\[
 h=a_0n^{-1/(\kappa+2)},
\]
where \(a_0>0\) is fixed below. For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\). The isolated thin-site property and the definitions of \(\mathsf J_P\) and \(a_P\) provide \(x_h\in\mathcal B\) and \(t_h\in\{0,1\}\) such that
\[
 q_{t_h,P}(x_h,h)=a_P(x_h,h)\le C_mh^{\kappa}. \tag{25}
\]
Set
\[
 \psi_h(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_h)}h\right)_+,
 \qquad \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12}.
\]
If \(t_h=1\), add \(\eta_h\psi_h(X)\) to \(Y(1)\); if \(t_h=0\), subtract it from \(Y(0)\); leave the other potential outcome unchanged. The function \(\eta_h\psi_h\) is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz, its absolute value is at most \(Lh_0/12<L\), and the score law and conditional Gaussian error law are unchanged. Hence the perturbed law \(Q_1\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). By (24),
\[
 \lVert\tau_{Q_1}-\tau_{Q_0}\rVert_{\infty}\ge\eta_h. \tag{26}
\]
The two observed laws have the same score marginal. Conditional on an assigned-side score \(z\), their Gaussian means differ by \(\eta_h\psi_h(z)\). Direct evaluation of the Gaussian likelihood ratio and (25) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 &=\frac{\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}
   \int\psi_h(z)^2\,d\mu_{t_h,P}(z)\\
 &\le\frac{C_mL^2}{288\sigma^2}h^{\kappa+2}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{27}
\]
Relative entropy is additive under independent sampling, so
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le C a_0^{\kappa+2}.
\]
Choose \(a_0\) so the last bound is at most \(1/8\). The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), with the supremum metric and \(2\delta=\eta_h\), yields
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})
 \ge c n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}
 =c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}. \tag{28}
\]

For the pervasive class let
\[
 h=a_0\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For large \(n\), \(h\le h_0/3\). The pervasive thin-site property supplies an \(h\)-separated set \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) such that
\[
 M\ge c_Jh^{-1},
 \qquad a_P(x_j,h)\le C_mh^{\kappa}\quad(1\le j\le M). \tag{29}
\]
Its finiteness follows from global boundary entropy. At each \(x_j\), choose a side attaining the minimum in \(a_P(x_j,h)\), and perturb that side by a radius-\(h/3\), height-\(Lh/12\) tent, upward on side one and downward on side zero. The membership argument above gives laws \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_M\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). At \(x_j\), the target under \(Q_j\) differs from the zero target by \(Lh/12\), while every other tent vanishes there because the centers are \(h\)-separated. Thus the target curves are pairwise separated by at least \(Lh/12\) in supremum norm. The calculation in (27) gives
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le M}
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_j^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})
 \le Cnh^{\kappa+2}
 =Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n. \tag{30}
\]
Equation (29) implies \(\log M\ge c_{\kappa}\log n\) eventually. Choose \(a_0\) smaller if necessary so that (30) is at most \(a\log M\), with \(a<1/8\) as in \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\). Its multiple-law clause gives
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \ge c\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}
 =c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{31}
\]
The exact-Gaussian circular families in \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\) provide explicit experiments with the same information budgets.

We next give data-driven upper-bound witnesses for the infimum defining \(R_n\). Let \(s_n\) denote either \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) or \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). By \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\), for all sufficiently large \(n\) there is \(b=b_n\in\mathcal H_n\) such that
\[
 s_n\le b<2s_n,
 \qquad b/2\in\mathcal H_n,
 \qquad b\le h_0/2. \tag{32}
\]
Choose a deterministic maximal \(b/2\)-separated set \(z_1,\ldots,z_M\) in \(\mathcal B\). It is a finite \(b/2\)-net, and global boundary entropy gives \(M\le2C_{\mathcal B}b^{-1}\). Let \(j(x)\) be the least index satisfying \(d(x,z_{j(x)})\le b/2\), and define
\[
 K_{t,j}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t, d(X_i,z_j)\le b\},
\]
\[
 \overline g_{t,j}
 =\frac{\sum_{i=1}^nY_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t, d(X_i,z_j)\le b\}}
 {K_{t,j}\vee1},
\]
and
\[
 \widetilde\tau_{n,b}(x)
 =\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\overline g_{1,j(x)}-\overline g_{0,j(x)}\}. \tag{33}
\]
This is one estimator measurable in the sample and known geometry. Since the trace envelope gives \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\), projection cannot increase pointwise error. On \(K_{t,j(x)}>0\), every included score is within \(3b/2\) of \(x\), so (24) and Lipschitz smoothness imply
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j(x)}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)
       -\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le\frac{3Lb}{2}. \tag{34}
\]

We use the following elementary count bound. If \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\), followed by \(1-y\le e^{-y}\), gives
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)
 \le2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{35}
\]

For the pervasive rate, take \(s_n=r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). The polynomial lower-mass property, (35), and a union bound over two sides and the net give an event \(H_b\) on which every \(K_{t,j}\ge nc_mb^{\kappa}/2\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(H_b^c)
 \le Cb^{-1}e^{-cnb^{\kappa}}. \tag{36}
\]
For fixed scores, every nonempty set defining \(\overline g_{t,j}\) is a disk pattern in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\). Since
\[
 |\mathcal H_n|\le C\log(en),
 \qquad \sum_{r=0}^3\binom nr\le C(1+n^3),
\]
that lemma bounds the conditional expected maximum normalized residual sum by \(C\sqrt{\log(en)}\). Hence, on \(H_b\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[
 \max_{t,j}\left|
 \overline g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)
 \right|\ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(en)}{nc_mb^{\kappa}}}. \tag{37}
\]
Because \(nb^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log n\), the right side is at most \(C_{\kappa}b\). On \(H_b^c\), clipping bounds the loss by \(4L\). Equations (34), (36), and (37), with the exponentially small remainder absorbed into \(b\), give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_{n,b}-\tau_P\rVert_{\infty}
 \le C_{\kappa}b
 \le C_{\kappa}r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}. \tag{38}
\]

For the isolated rate take \(s_n=r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), so \(nb^{\kappa}\asymp b^{-2}\). Fix a side, choose \(D\ge C_m\), set \(u_\ell=\min\{1,D2^\ell b^{\kappa}\}\), and put a net center in group zero when \(q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_0\), and in group \(\ell\ge1\) when
\[
 u_{\ell-1}<q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_\ell.
\]
Only the first index with \(u_\ell=1\) can be terminal. Every center in group \(\ell\) satisfies
\[
 a_P(z_j,b/2)\le q_{t,P}(z_j,b/2)\le q_{t,P}(z_j,b)\le u_\ell.
\]
The centers are \(b/2\)-separated. Applying the isolated upper profile at radius \(b/2\), including the terminal group, gives
\[
 M_\ell\le C_{\kappa}\{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}. \tag{39}
\]
In group zero, polynomial lower mass makes the mean count at least \(c_mnb^{\kappa}\ge cb^{-2}\); in every nonempty group \(\ell\ge1\), it is at least \(D2^{\ell-1}nb^{\kappa}\ge c2^\ell b^{-2}\). Equations (35) and (39), summed over groups and both sides, give an event \(H_b\) on which every group-\(\ell\) count is at least \(c2^\ell b^{-2}\) and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}P(H_b^c)
 &\le C_{\kappa}\sum_{\ell\ge0}
 \{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-c2^\ell/b^2}\\
 &\le C_{\kappa}e^{-c_{\kappa}/b^2}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{40}
\]
The last bound follows because, for sufficiently small \(b\), the ratio of consecutive summands is uniformly smaller than one.

Conditionally on the scores, each nonempty residual average is Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2/K_{t,j}\). On \(H_b\), the two-sided Gaussian tail bound and a union bound within groups yield, for \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{
 \max_{t,j}\left|\overline g_{t,j}-\mathbb E_P(\overline g_{t,j}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\right|>zb
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le C_{\kappa}\sum_{\ell\ge0}
 \{1+2^{\ell/(\kappa-2)}\}e^{-cz^22^\ell}. \tag{41}
\]
For all sufficiently large fixed \(z\), the series is bounded by \(C_{\kappa}e^{-c_{\kappa}z^2}\). Integrating this tail and using the trivial bound one below that threshold makes the conditional expected stochastic maximum at most \(C_{\kappa}b\). Equations (34), (40), and the \(4L\) clipped-loss bound on \(H_b^c\) now imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 \mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_{n,b}-\tau_P\rVert_{\infty}
 \le C_{\kappa}b
 \le C_{\kappa}r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}. \tag{42}
\]

The estimator (33) is an admissible witness for the common infimum in \(\mathrm{def:expected\text{-}sup\text{-}risk}\). Thus (38) and (42) prove the upper bounds, while (28) and (31) prove the matching lower bounds. The circular nonemptiness specifications are supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\). Finally,
\[
 \frac{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}{r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}}
 =(\log n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The two classes have the same scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), so that modulus alone cannot determine the expected-sup frontier; thin-site multiplicity separates the two risks.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Its fallback event obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}\le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\}\), and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.
statements.justification: This closes the same-class upper and lower frontier in the pervasive polynomial regime while controlling the operational empty-admissible-set fallback.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially varying sup-norm estimator and an inhomogeneous band for a positive continuous univariate design, Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive adapts at one query point, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 uses known design density and global \(L^2\) loss; none handles vanishing mass on two assignment sides uniformly along a boundary with a same-modulus \(h^{-1}\)-site converse.
statements.consumer: The \(R\), Python, and Stata \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflows can use observed-count bandwidths that widen automatically in depleted boundary segments and have a specified safe fallback.
statements.proof_tex:
The partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and sharp assignment imply \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) if and only if \(T_i=t\). Inspection of \(\mathrm{def:empirical\text{-}counts}\), \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\), \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}bandwidths}\), \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), and \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\) shows that \(\widehat\tau_n\) is measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\), the known geometry, \(L\), \(\sigma\), and \(n\), and uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density.

Fix \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\), and put
\[
 r=\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the dyadic grid contains \(h_*\) with
\[
 r\le h_*<2r. \tag{43}
\]
Take a maximal \(h_*/2\)-separated boundary net. It has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}h_*^{-1}\) points by global boundary entropy. If a net point \(z_j\) is within \(h_*/2\) of \(x\), then \(B(z_j,h_*/2)\subseteq B(x,h_*)\). Polynomial lower mass gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PN_{t,n}(z_j,h_*/2)\ge nc_m(h_*/2)^{\kappa}. \tag{44}
\]
For \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\) gives
\[
 \Pr(N\le nq/2)\le2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n\le e^{-nq/8}.
\]
Applying this inequality to all center-side counts and using ball inclusion yields an event \(G_n\) on which, simultaneously in \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 N_{t,n}(x,h_*)\ge c nc_mh_*^{\kappa},
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}P(G_n^c)
 \le Ch_*^{-1}e^{-cnc_mh_*^{\kappa}}. \tag{45}
\]
Uniformly over \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\),
\[
 \frac{nh_*^{\kappa}}{\log(e+n/h_*)}
 \ge c\left(\frac n{\log n}\right)^{2/(\overline\kappa+2)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{46}
\]
Thus \(h_*\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) everywhere on \(G_n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\). The minimizing property of the selected bandwidth, (43), and \(nr^{\kappa+2}=\log n\) imply
\[
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}{N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))}}
 \le Cr. \tag{47}
\]

Condition on the scores. If \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(s=\min\{h_0,r_0/2\}\) for any \(r_0>0\), the one-sided restricted score measure satisfies
\[
 P_X\{X\in\mathcal A_t:d(X,x)<r_0\}\ge q_{t,P}(x,s)\ge c_ms^\kappa>0.
\]
Thus every boundary point belongs to both side supports. Lipschitz continuity and the trace definition give \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x)\). If the selected count \(N\) is nonzero, Lipschitz smoothness gives
\[
 \left|N^{-1}\sum_{i\in S_{t,x,\widehat h}}g_{t,P}(X_i)-\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|
 \le L\widehat h_{t,n}(x). \tag{48}
\]
Let
\[
 Z_n=\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\{Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\}|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\) and \(|\mathcal H_n|\le2+\log_2n\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\le C\sqrt{\log n}. \tag{49}
\]
Every selected nonempty set belongs to \(\mathscr S_n\). Since \(h\le h_0<1\) implies \(\log(e+n/h)\ge\log n\), equations (47)--(49), followed by the triangle inequality over the sides, show that the conditional expected supremum loss is at most \(Cr\) on \(G_n\).

On \(G_n^c\), a selected set comes from either an admissible bandwidth or the fallback \(h_0\). The trace envelope and Lipschitz smoothness bound the conditional mean of every nonempty fit in absolute value by \(L(1+h_0)<2L\), while an empty fit is zero. Equation (49), with \(|S|^{-1/2}\le1\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 \le C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}. \tag{50}
\]
Using (45)--(50), and the common divergence in (46),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 &\le Cr+C\{L+\sigma\sqrt{\log n}\}h_*^{-1}e^{-cnc_mh_*^{\kappa}}\\
 &\le Cr. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{51}
\]
The constants are uniform in \(2<\kappa\le\overline\kappa\): dyadic factors are bounded by powers of two with exponent at most \(\overline\kappa\), and (46) gives a common diverging lower bound for the exponential argument.

The pervasive lower construction in \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), explicitly certified by \(\mathrm{lem:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}validity}\), applies at scale \(a_0r\). Its packing logarithm is bounded below by a fixed multiple of \(\log n\), uniformly over the exponent range, whereas the product divergence is at most
\[
 Ca_0^{\kappa+2}\log n\le Ca_0^4\log n
\]
for \(0<a_0<1\). A fixed sufficiently small \(a_0\) and \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\) yield
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge cr. \tag{52}
\]

It remains to verify the fallback probability. Take a maximal \(h_0/2\)-separated boundary net; it has at most \(2C_{\mathcal B}/h_0\) points. At every center and side, the expected radius-\(h_0/2\) count is at least \(nc_m(h_0/2)^{\kappa}\), which uniformly in the exponent range is eventually at least \(16\log(e+n/h_0)\). The binomial inequality derived above, a union bound, and ball inclusion show that, outside an event of probability at most
\[
 C\exp\{-cnc_mh_0^{\kappa}\}, \tag{53}
\]
one has \(N_{t,n}(x,h_0)\ge8\log(e+n/h_0)\) for every \(x,t\). Thus \(h_0\) is admissible everywhere and no fallback occurs. Enlarging \(C\), (53) implies the claimed \(Cn^3\exp\{-cnc_mh_0^{\kappa}\}\) bound. Equation (50) and the sharper event estimate (45) show that the fallback contribution is already included in (51). Equations (51)--(53) prove all conclusions.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.
statements.justification: This proposition removes a false early-kill premise before it contaminates the minimax theorem or the applied interpretation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate obtains a logarithmic pointwise rate under severe design degeneracy; the present proposition records the corresponding boundary-modulus sanity condition without claiming a new minimax theorem.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts will not mistake an extremely thin but positive region for a formally non-estimable boundary segment.
statements.proof_tex:
Positivity follows from the strictly positive integrand in \(\mathrm{def:exponential\text{-}modulus}\). With the substitution \(s=u^{-\alpha}\),
\[
 m_\alpha(h)=\frac2\alpha\int_{h^{-\alpha}}^\infty e^{-s}s^{-1/\alpha-1}\,ds.
\]
Let \(a=1+1/\alpha\) and \(x=h^{-\alpha}\). Integration by parts gives
\[
 \int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds
 =e^{-x}x^{-a}-a\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a-1}\,ds.
\]
The last integral is between zero and \(x^{-1}\int_x^\infty e^{-s}s^{-a}\,ds\). Hence the ratio of the first integral to \(e^{-x}x^{-a}\) lies between \((1+a/x)^{-1}\) and one and tends to one. Therefore
\[
 m_\alpha(h)\sim\frac2\alpha h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}
 \qquad(h\downarrow0).
\]
This proves the asserted two-sided asymptotic order.

For all sufficiently large \(n\), choose
\[
 h_n=\left(\tfrac12\log n\right)^{-1/\alpha}.
\]
Then \(h_n\downarrow0\), \(e^{-h_n^{-\alpha}}=n^{-1/2}\), and the preceding equivalence gives
\[
 \frac{n m_\alpha(h_n)}{\log n}
 \asymp n^{1/2}(\log n)^{-(\alpha+1)/\alpha-1}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus a fixed positive exponential modulus admits a vanishing bandwidth with diverging effective sample size and does not by itself force order-one risk.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
B_{t,n}(x)=
\begin{cases}
L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
L,&N=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then the data-measurable band
\[
\mathcal C_n(x)=\left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
\widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
satisfies, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\),
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
There is a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), \(P\), and \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), such that uniformly over \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) the band also satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)]\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover, for any \(\epsilon_n\ge0\), every band with simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma-\epsilon_n\) over a class containing laws \(P_0,P_1\) obeys, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_0}W_n(x)\ge
\frac{|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|}{2}
\left[1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-
\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\right]_+.
\]
Thus finite-sample global honesty, pervasive-rate global width, and a computable full-observed-law two-point width obstruction hold. This is a partial resolution: no uniform local-oracle width ratio and no necessary-and-sufficient criterion based only on score-law total variation are asserted.
statements.justification: This records the strongest proved answer to the honest-adaptation question: an explicit finite-sample honest band, its pervasive global-width rate, and a general full-observed-law two-point obstruction.
statements.gap: The proved calibration is global; it does not settle the sharper local-oracle width ratio or an exact necessary-and-sufficient adaptation criterion based only on score-law distinguishability.
statements.consumer: Applied boundary-discontinuity workflows can deploy the explicit globally honest band while reporting the unresolved local-oracle adaptation question separately.
statements.proof_tex:
Apply \(\mathrm{thm:global\text{-}honest\text{-}band\text{-}and\text{-}width\text{-}obstruction}\) with its displayed \(M_n\) and side radii \(B_{t,n}(x)\). Its first conclusion gives data measurability and, for each \(P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\),
\[
 P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Taking the infimum over the nonempty union preserves this bound. Since each \(B_{t,n}(x)\ge0\), the displayed interval has diameter \(2\{B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\}\). Hence \(\mathrm{def:band\text{-}half\text{-}width}\), as used by the preceding theorem, gives
\[
 W_n(x)=B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x).
\]
Its pervasive-width conclusion therefore yields
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}}
 \mathbb E_P\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}W_n(x)\right]
 \le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]

For the last clause, let \(A_j=\{\tau_{P_j}(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\}\). Coverage and total variation give
\[
 P_0(A_0)\ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n,
\]
and
\[
 P_0(A_1)\ge P_1(A_1)-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})
 \ge1-\gamma-\epsilon_n-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}).
\]
The union bound consequently gives
\[
 P_0(A_0\cap A_1)
 \ge1-2\gamma-2\epsilon_n-\operatorname{TV}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}).
\]
On \(A_0\cap A_1\), the interval contains both target values, so \(W_n(x)\ge|\tau_{P_1}(x)-\tau_{P_0}(x)|/2\). Multiplication by the positive part of the probability lower bound and expectation under \(P_0\) prove the displayed obstruction. These deductions establish exactly the three positive conclusions in the statement and do not invoke either explicitly excluded sharper assertion.

statements.statement: Let \(Q_0,\ldots,Q_M\) be probability laws and let \(v_0,\ldots,v_M\) be elements of a metric space whose metric \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}\) satisfies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_j,v_k)\ge 2\delta\) for \(j\ne k\). If \(M\ge2\) and \(M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)\le a\log M\), where \(0<a<1/8\), then every estimator \(\widehat v\) satisfies \(\max_{0\le j\le M}\mathbb E_{Q_j}\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge c\delta\) for a numerical \(c>0\). If \(M=1\) and \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)\le1/8\), the same conclusion holds. These conclusions also hold for product experiments after replacing each \(Q_j\) by its product law.
statements.proof_tex:
For the two-law assertion, let an estimator induce a nearest-point test \(\widehat J\in\{0,1\}\). On \(\{\widehat J\ne j\}\), the triangle inequality and \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(v_0,v_1)\ge2\delta\) imply \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_j)\ge\delta\). The smallest average testing error is
\[
 \frac12\int \min(dQ_0,dQ_1)=\frac{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)}2. \tag{11}
\]
For every measurable event \(A\), the log-sum inequality for the partition \(\{A,A^c\}\) gives, with \(p=Q_1(A)\) and \(q=Q_0(A)\),
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)
 \ge p\log\frac pq+(1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}
 \ge2(p-q)^2. \tag{12}
\]
The last inequality follows by integrating the second derivative \(1/\{p(1-p)\}\ge4\) of the binary relative entropy as a function of \(p\), whose value and first derivative vanish at \(p=q\). Taking the supremum over \(A\) in (12) yields
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(Q_1,Q_0)/2}\le1/4.
\]
Equation (11) and the nearest-point implication therefore make the maximum risk at least \(3\delta/8\).

For \(M\ge2\), let \(J\) be uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), draw \(Z\) from \(Q_J\), and put \(\overline Q=(M+1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^M Q_j\). Expansion of the logarithms gives, for any dominating law \(Q\),
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q)
 =\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 +(M+1)\operatorname{KL}(\overline Q,Q). \tag{13}
\]
Taking \(Q=Q_0\) in (13) bounds the mutual information by
\[
 I(J;Z)=\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=0}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,\overline Q)
 \le\frac1{M+1}\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{KL}(Q_j,Q_0)
 \le a\log M. \tag{14}
\]
For any decoder, if \(p_e=\Pr(\widehat J\ne J)\), conditioning entropy first on the error indicator and then, on error, on at most \(M\) alternatives gives
\[
 H(J\mid Z)\le\log2+p_e\log M.
\]
Since \(H(J)=\log(M+1)\) and \(I(J;Z)=H(J)-H(J\mid Z)\), (14) implies
\[
 p_e\ge
 \frac{\log(M+1)-a\log M-\log2}{\log M}. \tag{15}
\]
For \(M\ge2\) and \(0<a<1/8\), the right side has a positive numerical lower bound. Nearest-point decoding again implies \(\mathrm d_{\mathsf V}(\widehat v,v_J)\ge\delta\) on error. Averaging over \(J\), then bounding the average risk by the maximum risk, proves the stated conclusion. The argument concerns only the supplied laws, so replacing each by its product experiment leaves it unchanged.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\) and \(m(r)>0\) for every \(0<r\le h_0\). For every nonempty class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), let \(\overline\tau_n(x)=\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\{\widehat\tau_n(x)\}\), where \(\Pi_I\) is Euclidean projection onto the interval \(I\). There are constants \(A,C,c,a>0\), depending only on the fixed envelopes, such that
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \le C\min\left[ L,\ 
 \inf_{\substack{h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\\nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h)}}
 \left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}\right],
\]
with the infimum of the empty set interpreted as \(+\infty\). The estimator in this display uses neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\); they occur only in its guarantee. Conversely, if \(0<h\le h_0/3\), \(0<u\le1\), and \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\), then
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh
\]
whenever either \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), or \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\). Hence a sufficient uniform-consistency condition for a sequence of nonempty such classes with lower moduli \(m_n\) is the existence of \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that \(nm_n(h_n)/\log(e+n/h_n)\to\infty\); a necessary condition is that the supremum of the lower-bound-feasible values of \(h\) in the preceding display tends to zero. For a fixed positive exponential modulus \(m_\alpha\), the sufficient condition holds. With polynomial profiles, the lower display yields the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp1\) and the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) when \(M\asymp h^{-1}\); together with \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\), these rates are exact. For an arbitrary slack lower packing declaration, the lower display need not match the upper display based on global boundary entropy, so this is a proved two-sided bracket, not an assertion of an unproved exact arbitrary-profile criterion.
statements.justification: This theorem gives an explicit count-based global upper map and a legal same-class Lipschitz-tent converse indexed by the declared lower packing profile.
statements.gap: The two sides match in the isolated and pervasive polynomial regimes. For arbitrary declarations they can differ because \(\mathsf J_{-}\) may be slack while the upper argument covers the full boundary using global entropy.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can check the sufficient count condition before fitting and report a lower testing experiment when uniform consistency is impossible.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\), and define \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\). If \(x\in\mathcal B\) and \(r>0\), put \(s=\min\{h_0,r/2\}\). Positivity of \(m\) and the lower-mass member property give
\[
 \mu_{t,P}\{z:d(z,x)<r\}
 \ge q_{t,P}(x,s)
 \ge m(s)>0. \tag{54}
\]
Thus \(x\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) on both sides. The Lipschitz member property makes the specified representative continuous at \(x\), so
\[
 \theta_{t,P}(x)=g_{t,P}(x). \tag{55}
\]
The assignment partition and sharp assignment make \(X_i\in\mathcal A_t\) equivalent to \(T_i=t\). Hence, conditionally on the scores, each observed side average has mean equal to the corresponding average of \(g_{t,P}(X_i)\). The trace envelope gives \(\tau_P(x)\in[-2L,2L]\). Projection onto this interval cannot enlarge pointwise error, and the clipped loss is at most \(4L\).

We first prove the upper bound. Fix \(h\) such that \(h,2h\in\mathcal H_n\) and
\[
 nm(h)\ge A\log(e+n/h). \tag{56}
\]
Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_K\) be a maximal \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\). It is an \(h\)-net, and global boundary entropy gives \(K\le C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}\). By independent sampling, for each \(j,t\),
\[
 N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\sim\operatorname{Bin}\{n,q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\},
 \qquad q_{t,P}(z_j,h)\ge m(h). \tag{57}
\]
For \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,q)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(2^{-N}\), followed by \(1-y\le e^{-y}\), gives
\[
 \Pr\{N\le nq/2\}
 \le2^{nq/2}(1-q/2)^n
 \le e^{-nq/8}. \tag{58}
\]
Let \(H_h\) be the event that \(N_{t,n}(z_j,h)\ge nm(h)/2\) for every \(j,t\). Equations (57)--(58) and the union bound imply
\[
 \Pr_P(H_h^c)\le2C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. \tag{59}
\]
For any \(x\in\mathcal B\), choose \(z_j\) with \(d(x,z_j)\le h\). Since \(B(z_j,h)\subseteq B(x,2h)\), on \(H_h\),
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal B,\,t\in\{0,1\}}N_{t,n}(x,2h)
 \ge\frac{nm(h)}2. \tag{60}
\]
Choose the fixed constant \(A\) large enough that (56) makes the right side of (60) at least \(8\log(e+n/(2h))\). Then \(2h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\) for every \(x,t\) on \(H_h\).

Condition on \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\). For any nonempty averaging set indexed by \((x,b,t)\), (55) and Lipschitz smoothness give
\[
 \left|
 \frac1{N_{t,n}(x,b)}
 \sum_{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le b}g_{t,P}(X_i)
 -\theta_{t,P}(x)
 \right|\le Lb. \tag{61}
\]
Let \(Z_n\) be the maximum normalized error over the nonempty disk patterns in \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), with its zero convention. The exact conditional Gaussian hypothesis, as used in that lemma, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P(Z_n\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)
 \le\sqrt{2\log\left\{4|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^{3}\binom nj\right\}}+1
 \le C\sqrt{\log(e+n)}. \tag{62}
\]
On \(H_h\), every selected bandwidth is admissible and its set is nonempty. Conditional on the scores, it is fixed because it depends only on counts. For every candidate bandwidth \(b\le h_0<1\), \(\log(e+n/b)\ge\log(e+n)\) up to a fixed numerical factor. Equations (61)--(62) therefore bound the conditional expected side error by a constant times the selected criterion in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\). Its minimizing property and the admissible comparison bandwidth \(2h\), together with (60), imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n
 \right]
 \le C\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
 \quad\text{on }H_h. \tag{63}
\]
The two side errors and fixed factors from \(2h\) and (60) are absorbed into \(C\).

Projection does not enlarge error, and on \(H_h^c\) its supremum is at most \(4L\). Taking expectations in (63) and using (59) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})}
 \mathbb E_P\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\overline\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\\
 &\qquad\le C\left\{Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e+n/h)}{nm(h)}}\right\}
 +CLh^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{64}
\]
Increasing \(A\) so \(A/8\ge2\), (56), \(h\le h_0<1\), and \(n\ge1\) imply
\[
 h^{-1}e^{-nm(h)/8}
 \le h^{-1}(e+n/h)^{-A/8}
 \le h.
\]
Thus the last term in (64) is absorbed into \(CLh\). Independently of (56), the clipped loss is at most \(4L\). Taking the infimum over qualifying dyadic pairs, with the stated empty-set convention, proves the upper display. The explicit estimator definitions and the fixed projection use neither \(m\) nor \(\mathsf J_{-}\).

We next prove the lower display inside the same class. Choose \(P^\circ\) in the assumed nonempty class and retain its score marginal and geometry. On an extension carrying independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), define \(P_0\) by \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\). Every score-dependent member property is unchanged, while the side regressions and traces are zero. Therefore
\[
 P_0\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}). \tag{65}
\]
Let \(M=\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\ge1\). The lower-profile member property and the definition of \(\mathsf J_{P_0}\) supply \(h\)-separated points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\) such that
\[
 \min_{t\in\{0,1\}}q_{t,P_0}(x_j,h)\le u.
\]
Choose \(t_j\) attaining the minimum, and set
\[
 \eta_h=\frac{Lh}{12},
 \qquad \psi_{j,h}(z)=\left(1-\frac{3d(z,x_j)}h\right)_+. \tag{66}
\]
Retaining the score law and Gaussian errors, define \(P_j\) by shifting only the potential outcome on side \(t_j\): add \(\eta_h\psi_{j,h}(X)\) if \(t_j=1\), and subtract it if \(t_j=0\). Since \(\psi_{j,h}\) is \(3/h\)-Lipschitz, the perturbation is \(L/4\)-Lipschitz. Also \(h\le h_0/3<1\) gives \(\eta_h<L\). All design properties are unchanged and the residual about the shifted observed conditional mean remains \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\). Hence
\[
 P_j\in\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}),
 \qquad 1\le j\le M. \tag{67}
\]
Equation (54) puts each center in both side supports. The sign convention makes the causal contrast at \(x_j\) increase by \(\eta_h\), regardless of \(t_j\). For \(k\ne j\), \(d(x_j,x_k)\ge h\), while \(\psi_{k,h}\) is supported on \(B(x_k,h/3)\). Consequently
\[
 \|\tau_{P_j}-\tau_{P_k}\|_\infty\ge\eta_h,
 \qquad 0\le j<k\le M. \tag{68}
\]
If a conditional normal mean changes from zero to \(\mu\), direct substitution into the Gaussian densities gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{Y\sim\mathcal N(\mu,\sigma^2)}
 \log\frac{\phi_\sigma(Y-\mu)}{\phi_\sigma(Y)}
 =\frac{\mu^2}{2\sigma^2}. \tag{69}
\]
The perturbation is present only when \(X\in\mathcal A_{t_j}\), and the tent is supported in \(B(x_j,h/3)\subseteq B(x_j,h)\). Thus independent sampling, (69), and \(q_{t_j,P_0}(x_j,h)\le u\) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}(P_j^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})
 &=\frac{n\eta_h^2}{2\sigma^2}
 \int_{\mathcal A_{t_j}}\psi_{j,h}(z)^2\,dP_X(z)\\
 &\le\frac{nL^2h^2u}{288\sigma^2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{70}
\]
If \(M\ge1\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\), retain one alternative and decrease \(a\), if needed, so that (70) is at most \(1/8\). The two-law clause of \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}information\text{-}testing}\), with \(2\delta=\eta_h\), gives risk at least a numerical multiple of \(Lh\). If \(M\ge2\) and \(nL^2h^2u/\sigma^2\le a\log(M+1)\), use
\[
 \frac{\log(M+1)}{\log M}\le\frac{\log3}{\log2}
\]
and choose \(a\) smaller by this fixed factor. Then the average divergence in (70) is below the multiple-law threshold times \(\log M\). Equations (68) and the multiple-law clause give
\[
 R_n\{\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\}\ge cLh. \tag{71}
\]
This proves both alternatives in the lower display.

For a sequence of nonempty classes, suppose there are \(h_n\downarrow0\), with \(h_n,2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\), such that
\[
 \frac{nm_n(h_n)}{\log(e+n/h_n)}\longrightarrow\infty. \tag{72}
\]
The eligibility condition (56) then holds eventually, while \(Lh_n\to0\) and the square-root term in (64) tends to zero. The upper display proves uniform consistency. Conversely, let \(F_n\) be the set of radii satisfying either information condition in the lower display. If \(\sup F_n\not\to0\), then along a subsequence one can choose feasible \(h_n\) bounded below by a positive constant, taking a value above half the supremum when it is not attained. Equation (71) then bounds minimax risk away from zero. Thus uniform consistency requires \(\sup F_n\to0\).

For the fixed exponential modulus, \(\mathrm{prop:exponential\text{-}horn\text{-}consistency}\) gives
\[
 m_\alpha(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}e^{-h^{-\alpha}}.
\]
Set \(s_n=\{(\log n)/2\}^{-1/\alpha}\). Then
\[
 \frac{nm_\alpha(s_n)}{\log(e+n/s_n)}
 \asymp\frac{n^{1/2}s_n^{\alpha+1}}{\log n}
 \longrightarrow\infty. \tag{73}
\]
Because \(s_n\downarrow0\) and \(ns_n\to\infty\), for all large \(n\) it can be rounded upward to \(h_n\in\mathcal H_n\) so that \(s_n\le h_n<2s_n\) and \(2h_n\in\mathcal H_n\). Monotonicity of \(m_\alpha\) and \(\log(e+n/h_n)\le\log(e+n/s_n)\) preserve (73).

For polynomial profiles, put \(u=C_mh^\kappa\). If \(M\asymp1\), the first information condition holds at \(h\asymp n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\). If \(M\asymp h^{-1}\), then \(\log(M+1)\asymp\log(1/h)\), and the second condition holds at
\[
 h\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)},
 \qquad nh^{\kappa+2}\asymp\log(1/h).
\]
These lower rates match the corresponding achievability conclusions of \(\mathrm{thm:thickness\text{-}entropy\text{-}separation}\).

Finally, the generic displays can differ when the declared lower packing profile is slack. For the circular pervasive witness of \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\), take \(m(h)=c_mh^\kappa\) and declare \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=0\) for \(u<C_mh^\kappa\) and \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)=1\) for \(u\ge C_mh^\kappa\). This legal declaration exposes only \(M=1\) in (71), while the upper proof covers a global net of order \(h^{-1}\). Hence the arbitrary-profile result is exactly the claimed two-sided bracket, with equality of rates asserted only in the polynomial isolated and pervasive regimes already proved.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). For fixed score values \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\), let \(\mathscr S_n\) be the collection of nonempty index sets
\[
 \{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\},
 \qquad t\in\{0,1\},\quad x\in\mathcal B,\quad h\in\mathcal H_n.
\]
Then
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le 2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj.
\]
Under \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\) and the exact conditional Gaussian condition \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), adopt the convention that the maximum below is zero when \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\). For \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-almost every score vector, conditionally on the scores and with \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\), one has for every \(z>0\),
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}
 \frac{|\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i|}{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le 2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The conditional expectation of the displayed maximum is at most
\[
 \sqrt{2\log\{2(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|)\}}+1.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a score vector outside the \(P_X^{\otimes n}\)-null set on which either the conditional Gaussian assertion or the conditional product factorization below can fail.

First consider the deterministic trace count. For a closed disk with center \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\), membership of a fixed point \(X_i\) is equivalent to
\[
 2c^{\mathsf T}X_i+s\ge \lVert X_i\rVert_2^2,
 \qquad s=r^2-\lVert c\rVert_2^2. \tag{16}
\]
Thus every disk trace on \(\{X_1,\ldots,X_n\}\) is a sign pattern induced by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in the three-dimensional parameter \((c_1,c_2,s)\). A trace realized by a closed disk can be made strict without changing it: if some points are excluded, increase the radius by less than their strictly positive minimum distance from the disk; if none is excluded, use any sufficiently small increase. Equality in (16) therefore creates no additional trace.

Let \(A(n,v)\) be the largest number of open cells cut out by \(n\) affine hyperplanes in \(\mathbb R^v\). Adding the last hyperplane retains all old cells and splits at most \(A(n-1,v-1)\) of them, because the arrangement induced on that hyperplane has dimension \(v-1\). Hence
\[
 A(n,v)\le A(n-1,v)+A(n-1,v-1),
 \qquad A(0,v)=A(n,0)=1. \tag{17}
\]
Induction using Pascal's identity gives
\[
 A(n,3)\le\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{18}
\]
Restricting to genuine disks, fixing \(h\), restricting their centers to \(\mathcal B\), or intersecting each trace with the fixed side set \(\{i:X_i\in\mathcal A_t\}\) cannot increase the count. Multiplication by the two choices of \(t\) and by the finite cardinality \(|\mathcal H_n|\), supplied by \(\mathrm{def:dyadic\text{-}grid}\), proves
\[
 |\mathscr S_n|\le2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj. \tag{19}
\]

If \(\mathscr S_n=\varnothing\), the stochastic conclusions follow from the zero-maximum convention. Suppose it is nonempty. By \(\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling}\), the observed pairs are independent, so their regular conditional laws given \((X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) factor. Hence the residuals \(\varepsilon_i=Y_i-g_{T_i,P}(X_i)\) are conditionally independent. Because \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), an index in a side-\(t\) candidate set satisfies \(T_i=t\). The restricted score measure assigns full mass to \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\): using a countable rational-ball base of \(\mathbb R^2\), its complement is a countable union of basic open sets of restricted mass zero. Thus \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\) applies to every relevant index outside the fixed null set and gives
\[
 \mathcal L_P(\varepsilon_i\mid X_i)=\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2).
\]
Completing the square in the Gaussian density yields, for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[e^{\lambda\varepsilon_i}\mid X_i]
 &=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}
 \int_{\mathbb R}\exp\left\{\lambda u-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma^2}\right\}\,du\\
 &=e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}
 \frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}
 \int_{\mathbb R}\exp\left\{-\frac{(u-\sigma^2\lambda)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right\}\,du
 =e^{\sigma^2\lambda^2/2}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{20}
\]
For nonempty \(S\in\mathscr S_n\), set
\[
 Z_S=\frac1{\sigma\sqrt{|S|}}\sum_{i\in S}\varepsilon_i.
\]
Conditional independence and (20) imply, for every \(u\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[e^{uZ_S}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n]
 =\prod_{i\in S}e^{u^2/(2|S|)}
 =e^{u^2/2}. \tag{21}
\]
For \(z>0\), Markov's inequality applied to \(e^{zZ_S}\), followed by (21), gives
\[
 \Pr_P(Z_S>z\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n)\le e^{-z^2/2}.
\]
The same calculation for \(-Z_S\), and then a union bound over \(S\), yields
\[
 \Pr_P\left\{\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}|Z_S|>z
 \ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right\}
 \le2|\mathscr S_n|e^{-z^2/2}. \tag{22}
\]
No independence among the set-indexed sums is used.

Finally, let \(z_0=\sqrt{2\log\{2|\mathscr S_n|\}}\). Since \(|\mathscr S_n|\ge1\), one has \(z_0>1\). The tail-integral identity for a nonnegative random variable, (22), and
\[
 \int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\le z_0^{-1}e^{-z_0^2/2}
\]
give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_{S\in\mathscr S_n}|Z_S|\ \middle|\ X_1,\ldots,X_n\right]
 &\le z_0+2|\mathscr S_n|\int_{z_0}^{\infty}e^{-z^2/2}\,dz\\
 &\le z_0+z_0^{-1}\le z_0+1.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Together with the empty-family case, this is the claimed expectation bound with \(1\vee|\mathscr S_n|\).

statements.statement:
Under \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the residual \(\varepsilon_t=Y-g_{t,P}(X)\) is conditionally integrable and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]\le \exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\quad\text{for every }\lambda\in\mathbb R,
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]\le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]=g_{t,P}(z)\) at every such \(z\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(t\in\{0,1\}\). By \(\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}errors}\), there is a \(P_X\)-null set outside which, for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), the conditional law of
\[
 \varepsilon_t:=Y-g_{t,P}(X)
\]
given \(X=z\) is \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\). Fix such a \(z\), and write \(\varepsilon\) for a random variable having this conditional law. Since \(\sigma>0\), its density is
\[
 \varphi_\sigma(u)=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),\qquad u\in\mathbb R.
\]
For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), completing the square gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[\exp(\lambda\varepsilon_t)\mid X=z]
 &=\int_{\mathbb R}\exp(\lambda u)\varphi_\sigma(u)\,du\\
 &=\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2\lambda^2}{2}\right)
   \int_{\mathbb R}\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}
   \exp\!\left(-\frac{(u-\sigma^2\lambda)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)du\\
 &=\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2\lambda^2}{2}\right).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{1}
\]
The last integral equals one because its integrand is the density of a \(\mathcal N(\sigma^2\lambda,\sigma^2)\) variable. Thus the asserted conditional sub-Gaussian inequality holds, in fact with equality.

Absolute integrability follows directly from the same density:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[|\varepsilon_t|\mid X=z]
 &=\frac{2}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}
   \int_0^\infty u\exp\!\left(-\frac{u^2}{2\sigma^2}\right)du\\
 &=\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}
 \le \sigma\sqrt{2\pi}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
Here the integral is \(\sigma^2\), by the substitution \(v=u^2/(2\sigma^2)\), and the final inequality uses \(\pi\ge1\). Because the integrand \(u\varphi_\sigma(u)\) is absolutely integrable by (2) and odd,
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]
 =\int_{\mathbb R}u\varphi_\sigma(u)\,du=0.
 \tag{3}
\]
Finally, \(g_{t,P}(z)\) is finite because \(g_{t,P}:\mathcal X_{t,P}\to\mathbb R\). Therefore \(Y=g_{t,P}(X)+\varepsilon_t\) is conditionally integrable at the fixed \(z\), and (3) yields
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]
 =g_{t,P}(z)+\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_t\mid X=z]
 =g_{t,P}(z).
\]
The exceptional set was \(P_X\)-null, and \(t\) was arbitrary, so every conclusion holds for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and for \(P_X\)-almost every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\), as claimed.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). Put \(M_n=2|\mathcal H_n|\sum_{j=0}^3\binom nj\), let \(N=N_{t,n}(x,\widehat h_{t,n}(x))\), and define
\[
 B_{t,n}(x)=
 \begin{cases}
 L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)+\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2M_n/\gamma)/N},&N>0,\\
 L,&N=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Then the explicit band
\[
 \mathcal C_n(x)=
 \left[\widehat\tau_n(x)-B_{0,n}(x)-B_{1,n}(x),\ 
 \widehat\tau_n(x)+B_{0,n}(x)+B_{1,n}(x)\right]
\]
is data measurable and, for every declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), satisfies the finite-sample guarantee
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
